analysis: The PR raises NemotronSuperServingPolicy.maximumEncodedBodyBytes from 8 MiB to 40 MiB (NemotronSuperServingPolicy.swift ~line 369). NemotronSuperLocalImageBinding.encodedHeaderQuote now splits the guard: non-positive body, or a template outside (0, 1 MiB], still throws invalidInput, and a body above the policy bound throws the new Failure.bodyTooLarge. The size check still runs before any reservation, JSON parse, base64 decode or media decode, so it stays fail-closed. The ingress quote (body*32 + template*4 + 16 MiB) scales with the bound, to about 1.28 GiB at the cap. It is charged to the shared budget, and a failed reserve returns capacity (503). The one-media-request-per-owner guard (429) is unchanged. Mediacharge/videoMediaChargeBytes grow accordingly and the default prefix bank shrinks, a conservative direction for T-041. Code comments say the provider transports (localInferenceMaxUploadBytes, CoordinatorClient.maxInboundMessageBytes) are both 32 MiB, so the transports remain the effective cap and the real memory exposure widens less than the nominal 40 MiB. The new tests pin that these transport caps stay at or below the policy bound. SuperHTTPErrors.map adds .bodyTooLarge to MediaIngest.MediaError.mediaTooLarge with a constant message, so no prompt or media content leaks (A-001, T-008). The switch stays exhaustive. The prefix-cache crypto, scope, TTL and HMAC paths of T-041, attestation and authorization (TB-011) and the coordinator encryption boundary (TB-002) are untouched. I found no concrete regression. Residual, non-material uncertainties: the transport constants and the downstream status mapping (413 vs 400; the docs and tests are slightly inconsistent) are not visible in the supplied diff. Real peak memory versus the 32x multiplier is a pre-existing assumption. The quote's worst-case contention with concurrent text KV admission on small grants was not measured. These are documentation and correctness matters rather than security regressions.
